checks_performed: Compared sidebar navigation, st.page_link and st.switch_page
visible.message:
In my st.navigation app, a sidebar checkbox with key 'unit' lives in streamlit_app.py. Navigating with the sidebar or st.page_link keeps st.session_state.unit, but clicking a button that calls st.switch_page('page_1.py') loses it: AttributeError: st.session_state has no attribute "unit". Code:

# streamlit_app.py
st.sidebar.checkbox('set unit to True', key='unit')
pg = st.navigation({'Your app': [st.Page('page_1.py'), st.Page('page_2.py')]})
pg.run()

# page_2.py
if st.button('< Back to Page 1'):
    st.switch_page('page_1.py')

Streamlit 1.44.1, Python 3.11, macOS, Chrome. It used to work in a previous version.

agent_script.user_draft: The multipage guide says a widget executed in the entrypoint file stays stateful as users switch pages, so losing 'unit' only after st.switch_page contradicts the documented behaviour; I am passing your reproduction on 1.44.1 to a maintainer. As an interim workaround, the guide's dummy-key pattern copies the widget value into a separate Session State key that is preserved between pages.
agent_script.maintainer_summary: Docs say entrypoint widgets stay stateful; switch_page loses the key on 1.44.1. Interim: dummy-key pattern.
agent_script.rationale: Observed behaviour conflicts with the documented option 1; option 2 is a documented workaround.

evidence_links.claim: Widgets in the entrypoint file remain stateful as users switch pages.
Copy a widget value into a separate key to preserve it between pages.

decision_conditions.escalate: Name the conflict with the documented entrypoint behaviour and escalate; offering the dummy-key workaround is a plus.
decision_conditions.answer: Only if it gives the documented dummy-key workaround and states the switch_page loss is unexplained by the docs.

unacceptable_claims: The docs say st.switch_page clears widget state by design.
Moving the checkbox into the entrypoint fixes it (it is already there).
The user uses the pages/ directory.
